Ads will launch in Apple Maps in the United States and Canada later this summer. To mark the upcoming rollout, Apple has shared more details about what Apple Maps ads will and won't allow.

Apple Maps ads are coming, and Apple has revealed the banned categories

Apple first announced its plans to introduce ads in Apple Maps back in March. The company said ads would appear at the top of search results, as well as in a new "Suggested Places" widget within the app.

Apple laid the groundwork for this back in May with iOS 26.5, which included the new Suggested Places feature. However, the company has been quiet on when Apple Maps ads will actually launch since then.

According to TechCrunch, Apple has now updated its Apple Advertising Services guidelines with new information about Apple Maps.

The guidelines cover advertising across Apple News, Stocks, and Maps, and list a lengthy set of content prohibited across all services, including violence, weapons, and drugs, among others.

But the most notable detail is further information about the restrictions on Apple Maps ads specifically. Apple says Apple Maps ads additionally prohibit three categories:

  • Home services: Ads that include or directly or indirectly promote home services, including but not limited to plumbing, locksmith, HVAC, pest control, roofing, or general contracting services.
  • Bail bonds: Ads that include or directly or indirectly promote bail bond or surety bond services related to pretrial release in criminal cases.
  • Crypto ATMs: Ads that include or directly or indirectly promote crypto ATMs.

Additionally, Apple says ads related to medical services will be reviewed on a "case-by-case" basis.

As TechCrunch points out, Apple's blanket ban on the entire "home services" category of ads is notable. This is a major ad category on Google Maps, but Apple seems to have no interest in introducing it to Apple Maps.

All signs point to Apple launching ads in Apple Maps in the near future, but there's still no official launch date as of now.

For a full list of all ad categories banned across Apple's services, you can check out the company's website.
